text: Lesson 8 covered Lightning App Builder's canvas at the component level — whole list views, whole related lists. This lesson takes that same canvas one level deeper, down to the individual field, with a feature called Dynamic Forms.

Here's the old way, before Dynamic Forms. Every field on the record lives inside one monolithic Details tab, entirely controlled by the page layout. It's all-or-nothing — every user assigned that layout sees every field in that tab, in that order, no exceptions.

Migrate to Dynamic Forms and that same page gets broken apart. Each field, and each section, becomes its own individual component sitting directly on the Lightning App Builder canvas — placeable anywhere, configurable on its own.

Here's what that actually buys you. Because a field is now its own component, it can carry its own visibility rule. This filter only displays the field when Amount is one million dollars or more — no Apex, no validation rule hack, just a filter set directly on the component.

Before Dynamic Forms, one page layout meant one experience for every user, and conditional visibility needed real code. After Dynamic Forms, each field carries its own rule — different sales reps can see different fields on the exact same record, same page, zero code.

This is one of the most-tested App Builder features on the exam, and it's fully declarative and fully reversible. Next lesson: actions and quick actions, giving users a shortcut instead of a full record edit.
